purpose: Test mandatory conventional PHY while a separate timed-out MPS NeuralRx client continues physical GPU execution across the current and possibly later releases.

selection_source.remaining_gap: The earlier S2 controller called NeuralRx and conventional sequentially in one process, so cutoff did not leave a physically running optional client.
selection_source.smoke26: At cap100, a 40-graph unit averaged 44.96 ms; at cap20 it averaged 126.96 ms and remained active across later releases. Both 100-release smoke runs had zero D25 misses.

optional_fault.work_unit: 40 sequential persistent NeuralRx CUDA Graph launches
optional_fault.attempt_frequency: every 10th release when no previous unit is outstanding

interpretation_limit: This validates the declared persistent NeuralRx overrun. It does not prove protection against arbitrary HBM/DMA pressure or a non-yielding single kernel, and repeated fault injection represents endpoint recovery for characterization rather than continued admission of a known-bad client.
